clue.text: Dental work recalled by man with crown and filling

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the dental word runs backwards

parts.note: a cap is a crown fitted over a tooth
a king is a man who wears a crown

explanation.surface: A dentist's visit: a crown put on and a cavity filled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns CAP into PAC; 'filling' looks like more dental work but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Packing is material stuffed into a space, a synonym of filling in the sense of padding.

clue.text: Father's attempt to make dough

parts.note: pa is father, with the possessive s
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Dad has a go at making bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry is a dough of flour, fat and water used for pies and tarts.

clue.text: Poor game of cards with clubs leading

indicators.note: leading means coming first, before the card game

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
rummy is a card game

explanation.surface: A dismal card game in which clubs lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Crummy is informal for shoddy or inferior, a synonym of poor in quality.

clue.text: Wearing animal product, I provoked date to be incensed

parts.note: wearing something is being in it
fur is a product taken from animals

indicators.note: provoked means stirred up, so the letters of date are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone in a fur coat angered their date, who became furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Incensed and infuriated both mean made very angry, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Cunning guy is Leo, shaking all tails

indicators.note: shaking all tails means shaking off the last letter of every word

explanation.surface: A wily man born under Leo shaking his tail like a lion.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the last letter of GUY, IS and LEO leaves GU, I and LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Guile is crafty deceit, the noun for cunning in the sense of slyness.

clue.text: Company passes over 100 ancient documents

indicators.note: over is read as lying across or covering, so the verb surrounds the numeral

parts.note: passes, as in passes away, means dies
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A firm hands over a hundred old manuscripts.
explanation.definitionFit: A codex is an old manuscript book, so the plural names ancient bound documents.

clue.text: Beat trick question, shunning unknown journalist

parts.note: to con is to trick

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding, so the unknown letter is left out

parts.note: a query is a question
Y is an algebraic unknown
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A trick question beat a journalist who knew nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat in the sense of defeated means overcame, a synonym of the past tense here.

clue.text: Bird ousting rook from collective group

indicators.note: ousting means throwing out, so the chess letter is removed

parts.note: a drove is a herd of animals driven together
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A bird drives a rook out of the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rook' looks like part of the bird theme but is the chess piece, R.
explanation.definitionFit: The dove is a bird of the pigeon family, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Match in competition that is a beauty

indicators.note: in puts the match word inside the competition word

parts.note: a cup is a competition such as the FA Cup
a tie is a match in a knockout competition
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A cup tie that turns out to be a real stunner of a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie pie is an endearing or attractive person, an informal term for a beauty.

clue.text: Prepared target within second year for long-term plan

indicators.note: within means the jumbled letters sit between the two abbreviations
prepared means made ready, so the letters of target are reworked

explanation.surface: A target set out for the next couple of years as a long-term plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared' looks like an adjective for the target, but it signals the rearrangement; 'second year' is two abbreviations, not a school year.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is an overall plan designed to achieve a long-range aim.

clue.text: Mostly prudish crowd

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: stuffy means prim and strait-laced

explanation.surface: Describes a crowd of people who are, for the most part, prim.
explanation.definitionFit: To crowd a space is to cram or pack it full, the verb sense of stuff.

clue.text: Pioneer not vain or fake

indicators.note: fake signals that the letters of the phrase are counterfeited into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A trailblazer who is modest and genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is someone who introduces new methods, which is what an innovator does.

clue.text: Sorry about bit of food covering fine uniform

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: covering means the food word wraps round the two letters

parts.note: a morsel is a small bite of food
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An apology about a scrap of food that soiled a nice uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sorry for a wrong is feeling remorse, so the adjective is a synonym.

clue.text: Enthusiasm in Aztec site regularly displayed

indicators.note: regularly displayed means every other letter of the phrase is shown

explanation.surface: Keenness shown at an Aztec ruin, as tourists visit it.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of AZTEC SITE spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is gusto or keen relish, a direct synonym of enthusiasm.

clue.text: Caution welcoming band to northern town

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the caution word encloses the others

parts.note: to caution is to warn
a ring is a band, as worn on a finger
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning greets a band touring up north.
explanation.walkthrough: WARRINGTON is a town in Cheshire, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Warrington is a large town in north-west England, an example of a northern town.

clue.text: Punishing head of gang after second burglary

indicators.note: after places the gang's first letter behind the other two pieces

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it
a break-in is a burglary

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A gang leader's sentence handed down after a second burglary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' is the verb meaning support, not a unit of time or the letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: Backbreaking work is gruelling and exhausting, just as a punishing schedule is.

clue.text: Hold back tense horse after a butcher's turned up

indicators.note: after puts the tense and horse pieces behind the reversed look
turned up in a down clue means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a butcher's is a look, from Cockney rhyming slang butcher's hook, so a peek
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a bay is a reddish-brown horse

explanation.surface: A nervous horse, after a butcher appears, is restrained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a butcher's' is rhyming slang (butcher's hook = look), so A PEEK; 'turned up' reverses it to KEEPA.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something at bay is to hold it off or prevent it from advancing.

clue.text: Miner losing home gives up car

indicators.note: losing means the home word is taken away from miner

parts.note: in means at home
to cede is to surrender or give up

explanation.surface: A miner who loses his house surrenders his car.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercedes is the German make of luxury car, so it is an example of a car.

clue.text: Suggestion bizarrely so popular, to leave university

indicators.note: bizarrely means strangely, so the letters are rearranged
to leave means the university letter departs from the mix

explanation.surface: An odd idea that is very popular, about dropping out of college.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove U from SO POPULAR and rearrange the rest, signalled by 'bizarrely' and 'to leave'.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is a plan put forward for consideration, a synonym of suggestion.

clue.text: Rendered safe after ordering protective wear

indicators.note: ordering means the letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Something made safe once rules are imposed, then worn for protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Ear defenders are padded muffs worn to protect hearing from loud noise, a kind of protective gear.

clue.text: At start of battle, supporting mounted men with hearts pulsating

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means sitting underneath the earlier pieces

parts.note: H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts

indicators.note: mounted in a down clue means climbing, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Cavalry riding into battle with their hearts pounding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted men' suggests cavalry but gives OR (other ranks) reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Athrob means throbbing, beating rhythmically, so it describes something pulsating.

clue.text: Farewells from a Parisian couple hugging one

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping around, so the French number encloses the numeral

parts.note: deux is French for two, a couple
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Goodbyes from a French pair embracing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French goodbye, borrowed into English; this is its plural.

clue.text: Batman has one crime curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a caper is an audacious criminal escapade

explanation.surface: Batman tackles a crime that is stopped short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batman has one' reads as part of a story about crime-fighting but is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Batman's costume includes a long cloak, so the garment is something he famously has.

clue.text: Joined with friend inside and plotted

indicators.note: inside places the friend word within the joined word

parts.note: mated means coupled or joined
china means mate, from Cockney rhyming slang china plate

explanation.surface: Someone teamed up with a pal on the inside and schemed.
explanation.walkthrough: CHINA = friend is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate.
explanation.definitionFit: To machinate is to scheme or plot, so the past tense matches plotted.

clue.text: Wounds seen in hospital wings

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
arms are the side wings of a building or organisation

explanation.surface: Injuries treated in the hospital's wards.
explanation.definitionFit: To wound someone is to hurt or injure them, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Forceful people in films turned some characters for inside job

indicators.note: turned means the picked letters are read backwards
some characters means only some of the letters of the phrase are taken

explanation.surface: Tough characters in films reversing their roles for a heist.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Wars knights wield the Force, so they are wittily called forceful people in the films.

clue.text: Break up sad initially, overwhelmed by faint remnant of passion

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means swallowed up inside the faint word

parts.note: dim means faint

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: an ember is a glowing remnant of a fire, figuratively of a passion

explanation.surface: A sad parting, swamped by the last flicker of a romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break up' suggests a relationship ending, fitting the surface, but means tear apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismember is to cut or tear limb from limb, breaking something into pieces.

clue.text: 1 down is wrong, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word said for wrong gives the entry

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A claim that a cross-reference answer is incorrect, as rumoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 down is PASTRY; a torte is a kind of cake or tart.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich cake often made with a pastry base, so it serves as an example of pastry.

clue.text: A fly is buzzing around small edible plant

indicators.note: around puts the jumbled letters about the small letter
buzzing suggests the frantic movement of a fly, signalling the letters are jumbled

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A fly drones around a little edible plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buzzing' turns A FLY IS into SALIFY, and 'around' places it about S.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsify is a root vegetable, sometimes called oyster plant, eaten cooked.

clue.text: Make smooth punch? It's full of grains!

parts.note: to sand wood is to smooth it with abrasive paper
to box is to punch or spar

explanation.surface: A puzzled aside about smoothing a punch, as if it were full of grains.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's sandpit is filled with grains of sand, a cryptic description of it.
